title: Model of the magnon Kerr effect in a highly anisotropic ferromagnet
authors: Davit Petrosyan, Hiroki Matsumoto, Hanchen Wang, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, William Legrand
abstract: The magnon Kerr effect is a nonlinear phenomenon that occurs universally in any ferromagnet with finite magnetic anisotropy. It manifests itself as a magnon population-dependent change in the magnon dispersion relation. Here, we derive the Hamiltonian for the magnon Kerr effect for a thin film with uniaxial anisotropy. We consider the external field, parallel, perpendicular, and at an intermediate angle to the anisotropy axis, and determine the Kerr coefficient in each case. We show how the nonlinearity scales for different magnetic materials as a function of magnon frequency and magnetic sample volume. Moreover, we derive the equations of motion for a hybrid cavity-magnon system with such thin-film magnon Kerr nonlinearity, to obtain populations of photons and magnons, and scattering matrix terms for the microwave transmission of the cavity, relevant for experimental observations.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theoretical model for the magnon Kerr effect in anisotropic ferromagnets, deriving the necessary Hamiltonian for various external field orientations. It extends this theory to analyze the nonlinear coupling between magnons and photons in a microwave cavity, providing predictions for measurable quantities like the transmission spectrum.
main_problem: The paper models the magnon Kerr effect (MKE) in highly anisotropic ferromagnets, extending the theory to analyze its coupling with microwave cavities.
main_result: The MKE Hamiltonian is derived for various field orientations (OOP, IP, intermediate), and the theory predicts how the nonlinearity affects the coupled magnon-photon system's transmission spectra.
method: The authors derive the Hamiltonian using the Holstein-Primakoff transformation, linearize the equations, and then analyze the resulting anharmonic terms to model the nonlinear dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a thin film ferromagnet with uniaxial anisotropy coupled to a two-port microwave cavity resonator. The physics is governed by a nonlinear Hamiltonian incorporating the MKE, which manifests as a Duffing-type nonlinearity.
key_observables: Magnon Kerr coefficient (K), photon and magnon populations (|C|^2, |M|^2), and the microwave transmission spectrum ($S_{21}$ term).
important_parameters: External field orientation (parallel, perpendicular, intermediate angle), magnetic anisotropy constant ($K_u$), and the ratio of coupling strength to dissipation rate ($2g/\kappa_m$).
main_assumptions: The Holstein-Primakoff approximation is used, assuming small spin excitations. The anharmonic terms are simplified by keeping only terms of the correct order in the magnon operators.
figures_summary: Figures compare anisotropy energies in bulk vs. thin films, show the dependence of resonance fields and Kerr coefficients on magnetization angle, and plot photon/magnon populations versus drive frequency for varying input powers.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the Hamiltonian for the MKE under different field alignments (OOP, IP, intermediate), then extends the model to the coupled cavity-magnon system, finally analyzing the power-dependent dynamics and relating them to measurable microwave transmission.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it models nonlinear quantum dynamics (Kerr effect) in a solid-state magnetic system (magnonics) coupled to an optical/microwave cavity, bridging concepts from quantum optics and condensed matter magnetism.

FIG. 2. Thin ferromagnetic film magnetized IP in a mi- crowave cavity. The magnetization M of the film precesses elliptically around the external field Bext, with the ellipticity parameter ξ, and frequency given by the photonic excitation. The ferromagnetic resonance couples to the cavity mode with the coupling constant g. The cavity has two ports, with in- coming (cin 1 ) and outgoing (cout 2 ) photon amplitudes, and κcpl 1 and κcpl 2 are the coupling coefficients for respective port. The cavity has an internal dissipation rate κc, and photon ampli- tude C. The magnon dissipation rate is given by κm.

Spintronics.note: The paper directly models the nonlinear coupling between magnons (spin waves) and cavity photons via the magnon Kerr effect, which falls squarely into the cavity QED/magnon-photon polariton physics central to this research area.
